description:
memory.rs:340-358 — under the 'realistic-demo-ids' feature, demo_next_id computes:

  let base = *BASE.get_or_init(|| {
      SystemTime::now()
          .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
          .map(|d| d.as_nanos() as u64)
          .unwrap_or(1_000_000_000)
  });
  let n = base.wrapping_add(COUNTER.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed));
  Id::from(format!('{n:016x}'))

Issues:

1. SystemTime::now() can move backwards (NTP adjustments). The .map(...).unwrap_or(1e9) fallback handles the duration_since failure but does not handle SystemTime going backwards across two process restarts — a process started at T1, written to disk-equivalent ids near T1; a process started at T2 < T1 due to clock skew can mint ids that fall in the T1 process's range.

2. The fallback value 1_000_000_000 (1 second after epoch) is arbitrary and undocumented. The /// comment on demo_next_id mentions 'process-start nanos as base' without disclosing the fallback. A reader looking at id 0x...3b9aca01 will not know it's the fallback path.

3. wrapping_add can theoretically wrap if process runs >584 years. Cosmetic but the wrapping_add hides that the design has a finite cycle.

4. The unused-let-binding 'let _ = (inner, type_name, account_id);' at line 347 deliberately drops the per-account scoping. The doc comment says 'no type prefix, no per-account scoping. Lex-orderable globally within a process, not repeatable across runs.' That's documented, but it makes 'realistic-demo-ids' a different consistency model from the default — bad for testing because two test runs of the same code produce different ids.

This is a study impl; the warnings already make the demo nature explicit (memory.rs:322-339 are the multi-paragraph cargo-cult warnings). The fix isn't to make this production-quality, but to:
- Document the fallback value 1e9 and what triggers it.
- Mention SystemTime non-monotonicity in the doc-comment (RUST std docs already warn about this).
- Optionally use Instant::now().elapsed() relative to a single process-start OnceLock<Instant> for monotonic-within-process guarantees.

P3 — the demo nature is the dominant context, this is teach-by-example cleanup.
title: demo_next_id collision flag in 'realistic-demo-ids' mode silently uses time-based base; non-deterministic across runs
